phases.title: Today
phases.summary: A four-hectare patch of playing-field grass supports sport and meeting. The trees and track around it stay outside this example.
phases.tradeoff: The field already needs care and water. Its actual water sources and energy use are not established.

metrics.label: Demo area
metrics.detail: Authored subset of the Polo Fields, not the entire venue or a surveyed development plot.

metrics.label: Model irrigation
metrics.detail: No-build teaching allowance: 300 mm delivered to 4 ha each year; not metered park demand.

details: The campus is inactive. Existing park energy use is not established, not zero.
Optional rain replay: 86.4 mm recorded by NOAA San Francisco Downtown on December 11, 2014, about 5.8 km away. It is not an on-field observation.

phases.title: Lift the turf
phases.summary: A tractor strips grass from the work area. Some original turf stays; surrounding trees are left in place.
phases.tradeoff: Removing turf changes the place people use and adds fuel and supplied-water needs. Runoff at this transitional step is not calculated.

metrics.label: Turf removed
metrics.detail: Authored removal within the four-hectare demo area; no tree removal is included.

metrics.label: Selected diesel
metrics.detail: Illustrative selected equipment allowance over 10 workdays; not the whole construction inventory.

metrics.label: Work water
metrics.detail: Selected water supplied to site during this whole step; research teaching budget, not a measurement.

details: 10 selected workdays. The animation duration is not real elapsed construction time.
0.8 ha of original turf remains. The ground has not yet been graded.
Runoff is not established at this stripped-but-ungraded transition; it must not appear as zero.

phases.title: Shape the ground
phases.summary: Earthmoving machines grade the already stripped ground. Replay the same rain to see what the changed surface means for drainage.
phases.tradeoff: Preparing the ground adds work-water and fuel demand. More modelled runoff needs management; no lake pollution is calculated.

metrics.label: Selected diesel
metrics.detail: Illustrative selected equipment allowance over 30 workdays; not the whole construction inventory.

metrics.label: Work water
metrics.detail: Selected water supplied to site during this whole step; research teaching budget, not a measurement.

metrics.label: Rain runoff
metrics.detail: Modelled runoff during the same 86.4 mm daily rainfall replay; not an annual total or a flood prediction.

details: 30 selected workdays; two illustrative earthmoving machines. Hauling, water trucks and other plant are not fully inventoried.
The runoff method uses an assumed soil group B and the same rainfall at every phase. Actual field soil and flood depths are not established.

phases.title: Firm the ground
phases.summary: A roller compacts the same prepared area. It does not clear another patch of grass.
phases.tradeoff: Another step uses water and fuel. This research does not assign compaction an extra runoff increase.

metrics.label: Selected diesel
metrics.detail: Illustrative selected equipment allowance over 15 workdays; not the whole construction inventory.

metrics.label: Work water
metrics.detail: Selected water supplied to site during this whole step; research teaching budget, not a measurement.

metrics.label: Rain runoff
metrics.detail: Modelled runoff during the same 86.4 mm daily rainfall replay; not an annual total or a flood prediction.

details: 15 selected workdays. The original 0.8 ha of turf still remains.
Runoff is intentionally identical to the grading step under the prepared model; do not invent a compaction multiplier.

phases.title: Build the campus
phases.summary: Buildings rise on part of the prepared area. Construction needs supplied water, selected machinery and temporary electricity.
phases.tradeoff: Water used on site and water mixed into concrete elsewhere are separate. These are selected allowances, not a complete construction footprint.

metrics.label: Roof footprint
metrics.detail: Authored building roof area, not an inferred server capacity or total floor area.

metrics.label: Selected electricity
metrics.detail: Illustrative selected temporary-power allowance over 160 workdays.

metrics.label: Selected diesel
metrics.detail: Illustrative selected equipment allowance over 160 workdays; not the whole construction inventory.

details: 160 selected workdays. 2 ha remains bare and 0.8 ha remains original turf at this stage.
Selected water supplied on site: 1,988 m³ for this whole step.
Selected offsite concrete-mixing water: 1,080 m³, kept separate from site supply.
Contained washwater is illustrated; an unverified discharge to a park lake is not.

phases.title: Get ready to open
phases.summary: Cooling equipment and electrical tests come online. A roof tank captures part of the rain; the rest still needs managed drainage.
phases.tradeoff: Storage helps with one rainfall event. It does not create an annual water supply or prove the utilities have spare capacity.

metrics.label: Selected test electricity
metrics.detail: Illustrative selected grid tests over ten commissioning workdays; generator-test fuel is unknown.

metrics.label: Roof rain captured
metrics.detail: Capture from the same 86.4 mm event, with the 200 m³ tank starting empty and no within-event release or reuse.

metrics.label: Onward drainage
metrics.detail: Modelled volume needing managed drainage during this event; no peak-flow or flood-protection claim.

details: Final surface mix: 1.2 ha roofs, 1.6 ha hard surfaces, 0.4 ha restored landscape and 0.8 ha retained turf.
Selected supplied water for this commissioning step: 215 m³.
Actual utility connection, spare capacity and full commissioning inventory are not established.

phases.title: Switch it on
phases.summary: Computing needs electricity and cooling every day. Follow the water and power paths, then explore three possible changes.
phases.tradeoff: Supporting systems also use power. Some cooling water evaporates and some becomes managed wastewater; shared-system capacity is not assessed.

metrics.label: Average facility demand
metrics.detail: Annual-average electrical demand at the selected PUE, not peak load or connection rating.

metrics.label: Facility electricity
metrics.detail: First full 365-day operating year: IT plus all supporting systems; not cooling alone.

metrics.label: Cooling water supplied
metrics.detail: Annual-average cooling make-up, not a hot-day peak. Domestic supply and irrigation are separate.

details: Average IT electricity demand: 10 MW. It is already an average; do not apply utilization a second time.
IT electricity: 87.60 GWh/year. Supporting systems: 17.52 GWh/year, including cooling, electrical losses and other systems.
Cooling water: 225 m³/day evaporates and 75 m³/day becomes blowdown to an assumed managed sanitary connection.
All-source supplied water in the first operating year: 114,195 m³. This is supplied volume, not net consumptive use.
The three proposal previews are qualitative; no heat-delivery, recycled-water or green-roof savings have been calculated.

assumptions: Fictional educational campus on a schematic four-hectare grass subset of Polo Fields; not an actual development proposal or surveyed fit.
3.2 ha of turf is disturbed; surrounding trees and track are excluded. New planting does not replace public playing space.
10 MW is average IT demand. The transferred annual electrical PUE is 1.20; neither is measured Polo Fields performance.
Cooling make-up is an assumed 1.25 L/kWh IT with concentration ratio 4; coastal-climate performance is unverified.
The rain replay uses a real nearby station observation with assumed soil and runoff conditions; it is not a reconstruction or flood forecast.
A replay restores a complete phase. It never adds water, fuel or electricity to an accumulated score.
Heat reuse, recycled water and a green roof are visual concepts only. There are no numerical proposal benefits or combined savings.
